clue.text: A way that may get one into Hollywood film

definitions.text: A way that may get one into Hollywood
definitions.meaning: a famous Los Angeles street that runs through Hollywood
the 1950 Billy Wilder picture starring Gloria Swanson

explanation.surface: A route that might lead an aspiring actor into the movie business, plus a classic film.
explanation.definitionFit: The same name belongs both to the Los Angeles thoroughfare and to the celebrated 1950 film about faded stardom.

clue.text: Speak bluntly, as gunslingers do in westerns?

definitions.meaning: an idiom for talking frankly without careful thought
literally firing a pistol straight from the holster at the waist

explanation.surface: Talking straight is compared with how cowboys fire their guns in films.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for blunt, impulsive speech comes from the literal practice of firing without raising the gun to aim.

clue.text: Girl hammered at a nail

indicators.note: something hammered is beaten out of shape, so these letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is pounding away at a nail with a hammer.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's given name, a Slavic and Latin form of Natalie.

clue.text: Duke? Duke wife ignored

indicators.note: a thing ignored is left out, so the wife's letter is dropped from the duke's title

parts.note: the Duke of Wellington, victor at Waterloo

explanation.surface: A duke is asked about, and his wife has been snubbed.
explanation.walkthrough: Duke Ellington was the American jazz bandleader, so the first 'Duke' is a nickname, while the second is the aristocrat.
explanation.definitionFit: The jazz composer Edward Kennedy Ellington was universally known by the nickname Duke.

clue.text: One purchasing extra round university close to Manchester

indicators.note: the extra goes round the university letter, holding it inside

parts.note: a bye is a cricket extra, a run scored without the ball being hit

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A shopper is spending more around a university near Manchester.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a bye is one of the extras, runs not credited to a batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who purchases is a customer, the party paying in a sale.

clue.text: Let a nun be put out? That's indefensible

indicators.note: letters put out are disturbed from their places and rearranged

explanation.surface: Is it unjustifiable to evict a nun from her convent?
explanation.definitionFit: A position that cannot be held or defended is untenable, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Dissertation from Arafat, unfinished, turned up

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the letters are read from bottom to top
an unfinished word loses its final letter

parts.note: Yasser Arafat, the Palestinian leader

explanation.surface: A thesis about the Palestinian leader, left incomplete, has resurfaced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' cuts YASSER to YASSE, which 'turned up' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: A dissertation is an extended written piece of argument, the same kind of composition.

clue.text: A male criminal I nicked, going round

indicators.note: here 'I nicked' means I is taken in, captured inside the crook's word

parts.note: bent is slang for crooked or corrupt

explanation.surface: A crook has been arrested by the police while doing his rounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambient describes what surrounds or encircles, as in the surrounding air or atmosphere.

clue.text: Play in nasty joint

parts.note: a nasty situation is perilous or risky
a corner is a joint where two lines or walls meet

explanation.surface: A drama is being staged in a seedy dive.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1932 J. B. Priestley drama is named this way.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the title of a well-known stage drama by J. B. Priestley.

clue.text: Defeat (not in sport)

parts.note: someone not in is away from home or dismissed
to sport is to frolic or play

explanation.surface: A loss, with the parenthesis insisting it happened away from the sports field.
explanation.definitionFit: To outplay an opponent is to beat them by performing better, so it serves as a verb of victory.

clue.text: Key article on experimental weapons agreement

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another comes after it

parts.note: a test is an experimental trial
B is a musical key
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A crucial clause is being added to some experimental armaments treaty.
explanation.definitionFit: A treaty forbidding nuclear trials is a kind of arms-control pact.

clue.text: The Claw in short story being broadcast

indicators.note: a word cut short loses its final letter

parts.note: a tale is a story
a programme being broadcast is on air

explanation.surface: A short story called The Claw is going out on the radio.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird of prey's hooked claw has this specific name.

clue.text: Flowing by medieval English place of historical importance

indicators.note: one piece set by another sits next to it

parts.note: something runny flows freely
Med is an abbreviation of medieval

explanation.surface: A site of medieval English history beside a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: Runnymede, a meadow by the Thames, is where King John sealed Magna Carta in 1215.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the Thames-side meadow where Magna Carta was sealed, a landmark of constitutional history.

clue.text: Something to eat in bar, almost rare

indicators.note: rare suggests unusual, so the letters come out in an uncommon arrangement

explanation.surface: A meal in a pub, served nearly underdone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rare' looks like a description of meat cooking, but it signals the reshuffle of BAR ALMOST.
explanation.definitionFit: A roasted joint of young sheep is a classic dish, so it is something to eat.

clue.text: Film of Capone in European country

indicators.note: Al goes inside the name of the country

parts.note: Austria is a country in central Europe
Al Capone, the Chicago gangster

explanation.surface: A movie about the gangster Capone set in a European country.
explanation.definitionFit: Baz Luhrmann's 2008 epic starring Nicole Kidman bears the country's name.

clue.text: Start of number penned by jazzy trio?

definitions.text: Start of number penned by jazzy trio?

indicators.note: something penned by others is enclosed within them
jazzy suggests lively improvisation, so the letters are rearranged
the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A trio of jazz musicians composes the opening of a tune.
explanation.walkthrough: N, the start of 'number', sits inside ITRO, the rearranged letters of TRIO.
explanation.definitionFit: The opening passage of a piece of music is its introduction, often shortened to this.

clue.text: Bury one in a US city among other things

parts.note: to inter is to bury

indicators.note: the one goes inside the a plus the city

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Instructions to bury someone in an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the Latin phrase used in English to mean 'besides other matters'.

clue.text: Intend to protect good girl

indicators.note: a word that protects another wraps around it

parts.note: to mean is to intend

explanation.surface: Someone plans to shield a well-behaved young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's given name of Welsh origin, a pet form of Margaret.

clue.text: Tradesman less inclined to work after onset of gale

indicators.note: the second piece comes after the first
the onset of a word is its first letter

parts.note: lazier means more idle

explanation.surface: A workman who slacks off once the wind starts blowing.
explanation.definitionFit: A glazier is a skilled worker who fits glass in windows, a trade.

clue.text: Cry as a result of rows heard by outhouse

indicators.note: the second piece sits beside the first

parts.note: a shed is an outbuilding

indicators.note: heard means the word for rows is taken by its sound

parts.note: tiers are rows stacked one above another

explanation.surface: Someone weeps after hearing quarrels coming from the garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rows' reads as quarrels, but here it means ranks, tiers, which sound like drops from the eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: To weep is to let drops fall from the eyes, an idiom for crying.

clue.text: Misguidedly train as a mechanic

indicators.note: misguided means wrongly directed, so the letters are sent into another order

explanation.surface: Someone has unwisely chosen to qualify as a car repairer.
explanation.definitionFit: A skilled manual worker; in older usage a mechanic meant any craftsman.

clue.text: Senior teacher leading without thinking

parts.note: the head is the senior teacher of a school
to be leading is to be in first place

explanation.surface: The headmaster is in front, acting rashly.
explanation.definitionFit: Diving in this way means acting impetuously, an idiom for recklessness.

clue.text: Father round to prepare hobbit

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest
O is round in shape
to do a dish is to prepare it

explanation.surface: A priest goes round getting ready for a small fantasy creature.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolkien's ring-bearer, the hero of The Lord of the Rings, is the best known halfling.

clue.text: Lure one from agency over time

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece over another comes above it

parts.note: a temp is a worker supplied by an employment agency

explanation.surface: Coax an agency worker into staying overtime.
explanation.definitionFit: To entice is to draw someone in with an attraction, a synonym of luring.

clue.text: Relationship held in admiration

indicators.note: the letters are held inside the word that follows

explanation.surface: A romance in which someone is held in high regard.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics a ratio is the proportional relation between two quantities.

clue.text: Musical — Grease — or something from The Barber?

parts.note: Hair is the 1960s rock musical
grease is oil, a lubricant

explanation.surface: Two musicals, Hair and Grease, or perhaps the opera The Barber of Seville.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grease' looks like the other musical, but here it is just a lubricant.
explanation.definitionFit: A barber may dress a customer's head with this greasy styling product.

clue.text: Curse married woman

parts.note: Alison is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A wife is put under a spell.
explanation.definitionFit: Malison is an archaic word for a curse, the opposite of benison.

clue.text: Who could advise a sprinter on real running?

definitions.text: Who could advise a sprinter on real running?

indicators.note: running suggests motion, so these letters are set moving into a new order

explanation.surface: Who is the right person to coach an athlete on proper running technique?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines a fitness coach while its last four words, rearranged, spell it.
explanation.definitionFit: A fitness coach who works one-to-one could well advise an athlete on technique.
